title: Rainbow Valley

evidence.note: Renewal for a 1935 release would have fallen due in 1963. A fetch-based check of the Catalog of Copyright Entries motion-picture volumes for Jan–Jun 1962, Jan–Jun 1963 and Jan–Jun 1964 found no 'Rainbow Valley' renewal. The text was only partially readable, and the Jul–Dec 1963 volume was not checked. No Copyright Office public-records search was run. That is too little to call the print verified_pd.

watch.label: Rainbow Valley (1935) on the Internet Archive, uploaded by k-otic

editorial:
Rainbow Valley is a 1935 John Wayne western. Robert N. Bradbury directed, Paul Malvern produced, and Lindsley Parsons wrote it. Monogram Pictures distributed it. Wayne plays John Martin, a government agent working undercover, and Gabby Hayes and Lucile Browne appear alongside him. It is one of the B-westerns Wayne made in the 1930s, and its main appeal today is Wayne's early work. The Internet Archive hosts a copy, uploaded by k-otic.

The rights question is the renewal. A film released in 1935 stayed protected only if its copyright was renewed in the 28th year, which here means 1963. A partial look at the Jan–Jun catalog volumes for 1962 to 1964 turned up no renewal. The Jul–Dec 1963 volume and the Copyright Office public catalog were not searched. Until those are checked, treat the print as unconfirmed. The music, the story source and any modern transfer are separate questions that this research has not settled.
faq: Is Rainbow Valley (1935) in the public domain?

Not confirmed. A 1935 film needed renewal in 1963 to stay protected. A partial check of the 1962–64 Jan–Jun catalog volumes found no renewal. The Jul–Dec 1963 volume and the Copyright Office records still need checking, so don't assume it is free.
Can I use the Internet Archive copy in my project?

Only after the renewal check is finished. Even if the film turns out to be free, the layers are separate. The score, any source material and any added titles or music on a particular transfer could still be protected.
